To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for gender-affirming urologic surgery for my patient. This procedure is medically necessary and is supported by the World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH) Standards of Care Version 8 (2022), the American Urological Association (AUA), the American Medical Association (AMA), and the Endocrine Society.

CLINICAL SUMMARY

My patient presents with gender dysphoria (DSM-5 F64.0), a well-established medical condition recognized by all major medical and psychiatric organizations. The proposed procedure — [procedure name] — is medically necessary to treat this condition and has been recommended following a comprehensive multidisciplinary evaluation including mental health assessment, endocrinology consultation, and surgical evaluation.

All WPATH SOC-8 criteria have been met:
1. Persistent, well-documented gender dysphoria
2. Capacity to make fully informed decisions and consent to treatment
3. Relevant medical or mental health concerns reasonably well-controlled
4. ≥12 months of hormone therapy (if applicable and not contraindicated)
5. Mental health evaluation and clearance from qualified provider(s)

DENIAL REBUTTAL

If denied as "cosmetic": Gender-affirming surgery is not cosmetic. It is a medically necessary treatment for gender dysphoria (F64.0), a recognized psychiatric diagnosis. The AMA, AUA, American Psychiatric Association, American Psychological Association, and WPATH all classify gender-affirming surgery as medically necessary. Denial on cosmetic grounds is inconsistent with the medical consensus.

If denied as "experimental": Gender-affirming urologic procedures have been performed for decades with extensive long-term outcomes data demonstrating significant improvement in gender dysphoria, psychological well-being, and quality of life. These procedures are not experimental.

If denied due to plan exclusion: ACA Section 1557 prohibits sex discrimination in health coverage, which includes discrimination based on gender identity. Blanket exclusions for "sex transformation surgery" have been found to violate federal non-discrimination law in multiple court decisions.

EVIDENCE BASE

WPATH SOC-8 (Coleman et al., Int J Transgend Health. 2022;23(Suppl 1):S1-S259) provides the current international standard of care for gender-affirming surgical procedures, endorsed by over 60 professional medical organizations worldwide.

CONCLUSION

I respectfully request immediate reconsideration and approval of this medically necessary procedure. Denial of this treatment causes significant harm to my patient by prolonging untreated gender dysphoria.

Sincerely,
{{physician_name}}, {{credentials}}
{{practice_name}}
